message.content: Find the frontend module that contains memo CRUD mutations/queries (create, read, update, delete operations for "memo" entities). Look for files with names like useMemo*, memoService, memo queries, memo mutations, etc. Search broadly across the codebase. Also identify which generated service client it uses (e.g., a gRPC or API client). Search breadth: very thorough.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text: Now let me look at the connect module where the `memoServiceClient` is created, plus the additional memo-related hooks and the editor's memoService.

Here is the complete picture of the memo CRUD layer in this codebase.

---

## Primary CRUD Hooks File

**`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoQueries.ts`**

This is the central module containing all memo CRUD mutations and queries, built on **@tanstack/react-query** (`useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useInfiniteQuery`). It exports the following hooks:

| Hook | Operation | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `useMemos` | **Read (list)** | Fetches a page of memos via `memoServiceClient.listMemos` |
| `useInfiniteMemos` | **Read (list, paginated)** | Infinite-scroll pagination via `memoServiceClient.listMemos` with `pageToken` |
| `useMemo` | **Read (single)** | Fetches one memo by name via `memoServiceClient.getMemo` |
| `useCreateMemo` | **Create** | Creates a memo via `memoServiceClient.createMemo`, then invalidates list caches and user stats |
| `useUpdateMemo` | **Update** | Updates a memo via `memoServiceClient.updateMemo` with a `FieldMask`; includes optimistic cache updates with rollback on error |
| `useDeleteMemo` | **Delete** | Deletes a memo via `memoServiceClient.deleteMemo`, then removes from cache and invalidates lists |
| `useMemoComments` | **Read (comments)** | Lists comments for a memo via `memoServiceClient.listMemoComments` |
| `useInfiniteMemoComments` | **Read (comments, paginated)** | Paginated comment listing |
| `useLinkMetadata` | **Read (link metadata)** | Fetches link preview metadata via `memoServiceClient.getLinkMetadata` |

It also exports a `memoKeys` query-key factory for consistent React Query cache management.

---

## Generated Service Client (the gRPC/Connect-RPC layer)

**`/bench/repo/web/src/types/proto/api/v1/memo_service_pb.ts`**

This is the **protobuf-generated** TypeScript file (generated by `protoc-gen-es v2.12.1`) from the proto definition `api/v1/memo_service.proto`. It defines:

- The `MemoService` service descriptor with all RPC methods: `CreateMemo`, `ListMemos`, `GetMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, plus auxiliary methods for attachments, relations, comments, reactions, shares, and link metadata.
- All request/response message schemas (`CreateMemoRequestSchema`, `ListMemosRequestSchema`, `GetMemoRequestSchema`, `UpdateMemoRequestSchema`, `DeleteMemoRequestSchema`, etc.).
- The `Memo` type itself and related enums (`Visibility`, `MemoRelation_Type`).

---

## Client Instantiation

**`/bench/repo/web/src/connect.ts`**

The actual `memoServiceClient` used by all hooks is created here on line 197:

```ts
export const memoServiceClient = createClient(MemoService, transport);
```

It uses **@connectrpc/connect** (`createClient`) with a **@connectrpc/connect-web** transport (`createConnectTransport`). The transport uses binary protobuf format over HTTP (`useBinaryFormat: true`) with an authentication interceptor that handles bearer tokens and automatic token refresh. This is a **Connect-RPC** client (the modern gRPC-Web successor from the Buf ecosystem), not a raw gRPC client.

---

## Additional Memo Mutation/Query Files

1. **`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoShareQueries.ts`** -- Contains share-link CRUD hooks (`useMemoShares`, `useCreateMemoShare`, `useDeleteMemoShare`, `useSharedMemo`), all using the same `memoServiceClient`.

2. **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/memoService.ts`** -- A higher-level `memoService` object used by the editor. Its `save()` method orchestrates file uploads, then calls either `memoServiceClient.createMemo`, `memoServiceClient.createMemoComment`, or `memoServiceClient.updateMemo` (with a computed `FieldMask`) depending on whether the memo is new or being edited. This is the service that the editor's save flow uses rather than calling the hooks directly.

3. **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoView/hooks/useMemoActions.ts`** -- A small convenience hook wrapping `useUpdateMemo` from `useMemoQueries.ts` to provide a one-call `unpinMemo` action.

---

## Supporting Files

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/contexts/NewMemoContext.tsx`** -- React context for new-memo creation state.
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoFilters.ts`** -- Filter management for memo lists.
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoSorting.ts`** -- Sort-order management for memo lists.
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts`** -- Live/real-time refresh logic.
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoActionMenu/hooks.ts`** -- UI action hooks (archive, delete, pin) that consume the CRUD hooks from `useMemoQueries.ts`.
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/hooks/useMemoSave.ts`** -- Editor save hook that calls `memoService.save()`.
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/hooks/useMemoInit.ts`** -- Editor initialization from an existing memo.
